title: CrossBit: Bitwise Computing in NAND Flash Memory with Inter-Bitline Data Communication
problem: Existing in-flash processing (IFP) architectures can only perform bitwise operations on data sensed within the same bitline, preventing computation involving data from different bitlines. This restriction makes prior IFP designs unable to implement error correction codes (ECC) or efficiently process database query operations that require inter-bitline data interactions.
method: CrossBit extends commodity NAND flash memory with minimal additional circuitry to support both intra-bitline and inter-bitline bulk bitwise operations. It introduces inter-bitline communication pathways that allow data sensed from different bitlines to interact during in-flash compute. This enables in-flash ECC (IF-ECC) operations directly on MLC flash cells, which eliminates the prior restriction to SLC-only IFP. The same inter-bitline capability is leveraged to accelerate fundamental database selection and join queries that previously required data movement across bitlines.

title: 8.9 An On-Cell Monitoring and Balancing System with Near-Field Communications for EV Batteries
problem: Battery management systems (BMS) for EVs and grid storage require per-cell monitoring and charge balancing with reliable contactless communication and robust network formation, but traditional wired monitoring scales poorly with cell count (up to 216 cells).
method: On-cell distributed BMS architecture with per-cell monitor (CM) chips performing contactless serial communication to a system hub (SH); architecture includes per-cell processing, data storage, and charge balancing with network robustness through serial contactless protocol and dynamic network formation supporting up to 216 CMs per SH.

title: A UCIe Optical I/O Retimer Chiplet for AI Scale-up
problem: High-bandwidth AI accelerator interconnects require low-latency optical I/O solutions to scale multi-chip systems while maintaining signal integrity across chiplet boundaries.
method: Specialized chiplet implementing UCIe-compliant optical I/O retiming with integrated optical transducers and signal conditioning to bridge electrical and optical domains for chiplet communication.

title: 33.5 A 224GHz 19.9% TR Varactor-Less VCO Utilizing a Multi-Section Switch-Loaded Coupled-Line Resonator
problem: THz and sub-THz circuits require tunable elements like voltage-controlled oscillators (VCOs) and passive phase shifters, but varactors suffer from low Q-factor at frequencies >100GHz with limited tuning range, while switched-capacitor banks suffer from high OFF-state capacitance and low Q-factor.
method: 224GHz varactor-less VCO using multi-section switch-loaded coupled-line resonator achieving 19.9% tuning range through switched-inductor elements, overcoming varactor limitations and achieving high Q-factor at sub-THz frequencies.

title: DM-Tune: Quantizing Diffusion Models with Mixture-of-Gaussian Guided Noise Tuning
problem: Diffusion models require high computational and memory resources; traditional full-precision execution is inefficient; naive mixed-precision quantization adds runtime overhead from format casting and management complexity.
method: DM-Tune replaces complex mixed-precision strategies with a unified low-precision format augmented by noise-tuning fine-tuning. Noise-tuning reconstructs mixed-precision outputs via a parameterized nonlinear function (Gaussian + linear components). Framework identifies sensitive layers, models quantization noise, and provides custom low-precision GPU kernels supporting efficient noise-tuning.

title: Invited paper: Enhancing Design Automation with Quantum Algorithms for Chip Design
problem: Cell placement optimization to minimize Half-Perimeter Wire Length is computationally expensive in classical approaches, limiting scalability for large designs; quantum and hybrid approaches may offer speedup.
method: A flexible quantum-hybrid placement optimization strategy minimizes HPWL through both custom Simulated Annealing and D-Wave Constrained Quadratic Model solvers, integrated with OpenROAD flow for layout and routing; validated on ASAP7 7nm PDK with real-world case studies.

title: Late Breaking Results: Statistical Timing Graph Scheduling Algorithm for GPU Computation
problem: Statistical Static Timing Analysis (SSTA) handles on-chip variations by propagating timing distributions; computational complexity demands huge memory and runtime, limiting scalability to large designs.
method: Statistical timing graph (STG) scheduling algorithm for GPU execution; memory management strategy optimized for GPU memory constraints; tested on 18.2 GB STG workload.

title: Speculative Decoding for Verilog: Speed and Quality, All in One
problem: LLM-based Verilog code generation suffers from poor tokenization and decoding due to Verilog's specialized syntax and underrepresentation in training data, resulting in slow and low-quality code.
method: Applies speculative decoding with syntactically-aligned tokenization that breaks at syntactically significant tokens rather than subword units, enabling better capture of Verilog logical constructs.

title: Can Short Hypervectors Drive Feature-Rich GNNs? Strengthening the Graph Representation of Hyperdimensional Computing for Memory-efficient GNNs
problem: Hyperdimensional computing (HDC) requires ultra-long hypervectors (tens of thousands of bits) to express rich features, creating a memory bottleneck that offsets HDC's computational efficiency.
method: CiliaGraph rebuilds HDC operations to overcome three GNN incompatibilities: (1) feature distortion via better encoding, (2) structural bias via weighted aggregation, (3) central-node vacancy via expanded supervision. Uses short hypervectors (hundreds of bits) with error-tolerant neural principles to maintain accuracy.

title: GSArch: Breaking Memory Barriers in 3D Gaussian Splatting Training via Architectural Support
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) training is bottlenecked by three memory system inefficiencies: redundant off-chip DRAM loads for large 'hot' Gaussians accessed repeatedly across pixels, expensive atomic write operations during gradient accumulation, and severe bank conflicts during on-chip buffer reads during backward propagation.
method: GSArch introduces three architectural mechanisms targeting the three bottlenecks: (1) Hybrid memory management that classifies Gaussians as 'hot' (large, high pixel overlap, repeatedly loaded) or 'cold' and caches hot Gaussians in a fast on-chip buffer to eliminate redundant DRAM fetches; (2) Gradient informativeness filtering that identifies low-contribution gradients and skips their atomic write operations during backward propagation; (3) A rearrangement unit that packs conflicting on-chip memory read requests into non-conflicting bundles to eliminate bank conflicts. These techniques combine to accelerate the backward pass of 3DGS training.

title: Skia: Exposing Shadow Branches
problem: Modern processors using Fetch Directed Instruction Prefetching (FDIP) suffer from Branch Target Buffer (BTB) misses for instructions that have been previously decoded and evicted, causing the Branch Prediction Unit (BPU) to fail to recognize branches and either skip prefetching or speculate down wrong paths. These BTB misses stall the front-end and pollute the L1-I cache, a critical bottleneck for complex datacenter applications with large code footprints.
method: Skia introduces 'shadow branches': lightweight metadata structures that expose BTB-evicted branch information to the FDIP engine without restoring full BTB entries. When a branch is decoded and later evicted from the BTB, Skia retains shadow branch records (address and target hints) in a separate, higher-capacity structure. The FDIP engine consults these shadow records to continue speculative fetching along correct paths even when a BTB miss would otherwise halt prefetching or cause misdirection. This avoids both missed prefetches and wrong-path pollution of the L1-I cache.

title: A 232-to-260GHz CMOS Amplifier-Multiplier Chain With a Low-Cost, Matching-Sheet-Assisted Radiation Package and 11.1dBm Total Radiated Power
problem: Compact CMOS terahertz (THz) sources are limited by low radiated power (several mW); on-chip radiation via front-side patch antennas suffers low efficiency (~25%) and narrow bandwidth (~5%); back-side radiation improves efficiency but requires expensive silicon lenses (cm-sized, high-cost assembly) to overcome total internal reflection at Si-air interface.
method: 232–260GHz CMOS amplifier-multiplier chain with back-side radiation via low-cost patterned dielectric matching sheet (instead of silicon lens). Matching sheet enhances wave coupling from silicon (εr=11.9) to air (εr=1), improving radiation efficiency and bandwidth. Circuit uses high-power FinFET (HyPowerFF) technology and broadband gain-peaking power amplifiers.

title: H-Houdini: Scalable Invariant Learning
problem: Formal hardware verification via invariant learning (e.g., IC3/PDR) does not scale to large hardware designs because the invariant search space grows exponentially with state size, causing state-of-the-art tools to time out on real-world RTL designs.
method: H-Houdini extends the Houdini invariant-learning algorithm with scalability improvements targeting large hardware designs. The likely approach involves decomposing the hardware design into manageable sub-modules or abstract components, learning invariants compositionally (e.g., assume-guarantee or abstraction-refinement), and propagating learned invariants across the design hierarchy to avoid full-state enumeration. Specific algorithmic details are not disclosed in the available abstract.

title: Adyna: Accelerating Dynamic Neural Networks with Adaptive Scheduling
problem: Dynamic neural networks (DynNNs) conditionally skip computation based on input difficulty, but current GPUs and specialized accelerators lack dataflow and architecture support to realize the theoretical efficiency gains, because the dynamic execution patterns defeat static resource allocation.
method: Adyna uses a unified representation to model diverse DynNN variants and introduces a dynamism-aware multi-kernel selection paradigm. At runtime, a dataflow scheduler observes the distribution of dynamic size values (e.g., number of active tokens or blocks) and selects among multiple precompiled kernels, each optimized for a specific dynamic-size bucket. An effective kernel sampling algorithm chooses the minimal set of kernels to precompile and cache on the accelerator, balancing coverage against on-chip memory cost. The hardware architecture supports multi-tile and multi-tenant execution to handle concurrent dynamic workloads.

title: A 6.78MHz 94.2% Peak Efficiency Class-E Transmitter with Adaptive Real-Part Impedance Matching and Imaginary-Part Phase Compensation Achieving a 33W Wireless-Power-Transfer System
problem: Wireless power transfer (WPT) systems achieve high efficiency only at specific load points; load impedance varies significantly as charging state changes, causing both real and imaginary parts to shift beyond the circuit's operating range.
method: Class-E power amplifier at 6.78MHz with dual adaptive impedance matching: real-part adaptation via dynamic impedance matching network, and imaginary-part phase compensation via adaptive capacitance (avoiding nonlinear MOS capacitors), achieving 94.2% peak efficiency across wide load range.

title: UniCAIM: A Unified CAM/CIM Architecture with Static-Dynamic KV Cache Pruning for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
problem: Transformer LLM inference on long sequences suffers from massive KV cache memory and computation overhead; existing CIM accelerators support only static pruning with fixed patterns or inefficient dynamic pruning.
method: Proposes FeFET-based unified CAM/CIM architecture (UniCAIM) with three computation modes: 1) CAM mode for O(1) dynamic KV pruning via approximate similarity, 2) charge-domain CIM for static pruning with flexible patterns, 3) current-domain for exact attention on pruned KV. Leverages FeFET multi-level storage for signed multibit KV and in-place computation.
